actionable_steps: Pre-register the search in a committed PLAN.md (sample rule, holdout rule, period/duration grid, first-screen thresholds, null design, vetting ladder) before downloading any light curve; Kuber had to reconstruct this after the fact for the editor.

Reproduce the Kepler Bonus selection with the exact cuts (psffrac>0.5, crowdsap>0.7, >=8 PSF quarters, kic!=tpforg, drop keplerstellar kepids; expect 1,800) and decide explicitly whether to reuse this already-searched M-dwarf pool or widen to the 406,548 background sources with different cuts.
Ingest KBONUS FITS per quarter with PSFFRAC>=0.5, SAP_QUALITY==0, >=300 cadences, median normalisation, BTJD = TIME - 2167, and carry SAP_FLUX with SAP_FLUX_ERR (not PSF errors) from day one.

Implement the search as per-quarter wotan biweight (1.0 d) + two-stage BLS (or TLS) with rho prior, two peaks per star, and the pilot screen; run the inverted (2 - flux) control on every star the same night and report real vs inverted pass counts up front.
Run Kepler-138 (KIC 7603200) and a few faint KOIs as positive controls, and add a real injection-recovery completeness grid (Kuber never did one) to set thresholds instead of inheriting SNR>=9.

Port independent_vet.py (exposure-integrated per-event box + linear baseline, cluster-robust errors, leave-one-out, odd/even, secondary, phase controls, per-quarter depths, fixed-ephemeris holdout) and run it on PSF and SAP for every survivor.

For each survivor, download the aperture primary's Kepler TPFs and do PRF localisation (lightkurve.prf.KeplerPRF, proper-motion-propagated positions), raw centroid shifts, per-season difference images, and the FLFRCSAP dilution model; download neighbours' KBONUS light curves and test them at the fixed ephemeris.
Test every KOI/TCE/EB ephemeris within 5 arcmin against the event times (overlaps, nearest separation, period sigma, folded depth) exactly as k169_overlap.py/kdepth.py do.

Check novelty against KOI/TCE/EB, Kepler Bonus candidate lists, Bienias & Szabo 2025, APEXBA 2022, Barber et al. 2022 Table 5 and ExoFOP/SIMBAD, with provenance JSON per query; write 'no prior report found as of <date>', never 'never searched'.

Fit batman+emcee with exposure integration and red-noise inflation on both extractions; run TRICERATOPS 1.1 offline with the Kepler exposure time and a Gaia-cone background, passing resolved neighbours with aperture flux ratios so NFPP is meaningful, plus a MOLUSC/RUWE companion prior and LEO-Vetter flux tests.

Publish a dated, hashed evidence pack (search/, validation/, provenance JSONs, requirements-lock, positive and inverted outputs, LLM-entry-point rules) with a Zenodo DOI, and call the result a 'planet candidate' unless FPP<0.015 and NFPP<0.001.

Before any journal submission or public post, get an astronomer to read the pack and resolve any prior-search flag; expect RNAAS to decline an unvalidated single-candidate note and plan for arXiv-plus-DOI or co-authorship with a group that can obtain AO imaging.
